title: Excluded middle for propositions, as Lean proves it
statement: For every proposition p, either p holds or its negation holds.

evidence.supports: `Classical.em`'s Lean proof term type-checks against this statement in the independent Axeyum kernel.
checkers: Kernel::add_declaration (independent re-derivation of the type from the proof term)
SHA-256 pin of the exported stream bytes
evidence.notes: The command greps for this fact's own marker line rather than trusting the exit status, so a suite that compiles to zero tests -- this repository's signature defect -- fails instead of exiting 0. Measured 2026-08-15: the stream hashes to the pin in `artifacts/lean-imports/MANIFEST.json`, the fail-closed importer admits 106 declarations (it publishes nothing unless the WHOLE stream translates and every declaration passes the trusted gate), and `Kernel::render_lean` of the admitted type is `((p : Prop) -> Or p (Not p))`. `formal.statement` is that string verbatim.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: the imported proof term reaches six trusted declarations in our kernel's classification, three in Lean's
checkers: Kernel::axiom_footprint (our kernel, over the imported environment)
evidence.notes: Two kernels, independently. `Kernel::axiom_footprint` walks this declaration's transitive dependencies in the IMPORTED environment and reports `Classical.choice, Quot, Quot.lift, Quot.mk, Quot.sound, propext` -- six names, because our kernel counts the whole quotient package as trusted `Quotient` declarations; a real Lean 4.30.0 binary's `#print axioms Classical.em` reports `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` -- three names. The first three entries are the assumptions the IMPORT adds and the constructed `kernel-lean` route does not make: that the exporter faithfully rendered Lean's environment, that our NDJSON-to-kernel-term translation preserves meaning, and that the delivered bytes are the producer's intended export -- format 3.1 has no footer, so completion is relative to the bytes handed over, which `axeyum-lean-import`'s own documentation states. They are why `axiom_footprint: []` is unavailable on this route and the validator rejects it (ADR-0454).

notes:
The reason to import this one is the footprint, not the theorem. Three things become visible that no other fact in this ledger shows.

(1) THE TWO KERNELS DISAGREE ON HOW TO SPELL A FOOTPRINT. Lean's `#print axioms` reports three names; `Kernel::axiom_footprint` reports six, adding `Quot`, `Quot.mk` and `Quot.lift` because our kernel classifies the entire quotient package as `Declaration::Quotient`. Both are correct in their own vocabulary, ours is the more conservative reading, and the disagreement is recorded rather than reconciled -- the same theorem checked by two kernels has two correct footprints of different length. Reconciling them silently would be the precise error `proof_route` exists to prevent.

(2) IT IS NOT `F:excluded-middle`. That fact is `(assert (or p (not p)))` over a BOOLEAN `p`, settled on `smt-term-level` by exhaustive evaluation of 2 assignments. This one quantifies over all of `Prop`, which no exhaustive evaluation can reach, and it is not intuitionistically provable -- hence the three Lean axioms. Neither fact supersedes the other and neither footprint is comparable to the other.

(3) IT IS NOT REACHABLE ON OUR `kernel-lean` ROUTE AT ALL. This project's logic prelude is intuitionistic and measured axiom-free, so excluded middle over `Prop` is unobtainable there without adding an axiom (ADR-0453). Importing it does not change that: what we now hold is a checked record of Lean's proof and its cost in axioms, not a constructed proof of our own.
